items.label: section_header
items.text: THE PERIODIC TABLE

items.label: text
items.text: Chapter 4 deals in detail with what you need to know about the Periodic Table for International GCSEpurposes.

items.label: text
items.text: Atoms are arranged in the Periodic Table in order of increasing atomic number. You will find a full version of the Periodic Table in Appendix A on page 320. Most Periodic Tables have two numbers against each symbol; be careful to choose the right one. The atomic number will always be the smaller number. The other number will either be the mass number of the most common isotope of the element or the relative atomic mass of the element. The Periodic Table will clarify this.

items.label: text
items.text: You can use a Periodic Table to find out the number of protons, neutrons and electrons in an atom. Remember:

items.label: list_item
items.text: the number of protons in an atom is equal to the atomic number

items.label: list_item
items.text: the number of electrons in an atom is equal to the number of protons

items.label: list_item
items.text: the number of neutrons in an atom = mass number - atomic number.

items.label: section_header
items.text: EXAMPLE 2

items.label: text
items.text: The symbol for uranium is given in a Periodic Table as:

items.label: text
items.text: 238 U Uranium 92

items.label: text
items.text: Calculate the number of protons, neutrons and electrons in an atom of uranium.

items.label: text
items.text: The atomic number is the smaller number, so the atomic number of uranium is 92. The atomic number tells us the number of protons, therefore a uranium atom contains 92 protons.

items.label: text
items.text: The number of protons is equal to the number of electrons, therefore a uranium atom contains 92 electrons.

items.label: text
items.text: The number of neutrons = mass number – atomic number.

items.label: text
items.text: The number of neutrons = 238 – 92 = 146.

items.label: text
items.text: You will need to use the Periodic Table in Appendix A on page 320.
